(Flower, headword 827 / code 893) and 'Fr.' (Fruit, headword 829 / code 895) are formally available, the verse and the numbering give no plant parts, and AFI's own printings of this drug are not uniform - '(F1.)' at lines 12696 and 12797, '(?1.)' at 25148, but '(Rt.)' at 21708 and 21866 - so the parallel printings do not force Fl. either. Manjistha", "3. Sarja rasa", "4. Sariva" — the last three names of the verse against numbers 2, 3, 4 — so the lost row 1 can only be madhucchista. NOTHING ELSE IN THE ROW IS CORRECTED: gloss, part and quantity are recorded illegible because the cells themselves are destroyed and no verse or numbering evidence fixes them. In particular the words "bees wax" are NOT recorded as this row's gloss: they occur only in the entry's prose Special method of preparation at line 20346 ("the shavings of madhucchista (bees wax)"), which says nothing about what, if anything, the composition table printed in the gloss cell. Non-forcing observation, recorded but not applied: elsewhere in this book the ingredient is printed as "Sikthaka (madhicchista)" / "Siktha (madhicchista)" with no part abbreviation (lines 12566, 12659, 19699), which makes an empty part cell plausible here — plausible is not forced, so the cell stays illegible.

rows.name: Sariva
rows.ocrCorrected: Line 20333 reads, byte for byte: "4. Sariva (इष्टय sariva) (२) 455 8." (the text after it on that line, "pravahika; परव nihsarana; = वाऽय;", is entry 8:29's right column). Three separate judgements on this row: (1) NAME "Sariva" is printed clean, no correction. (2) GLOSS ILLEGIBLE — the parenthesis holds garbled Devanagari "इष्टय" followed by a legible roman token "sariva"; the cell as printed cannot be read, and neither the verse ("ससर्जरससारिवम्‌" at line 20326, which names sariva and nothing more) nor the numbering fixes it. Non-forcing observation, recorded but NOT applied: every other Sariva row in this book prints the gloss "(Sveta sariva)" or "(krsna sariva)" (lines 3594, 4326, 12580, 13970, 19713, 21096, 21211, 21868, 33453 and others), so "इष्टय" is probably a mangled "Sveta" — probable is not forced, so the cell is left illegible rather than filled. (3) PART ILLEGIBLE — the cell prints as "(२)" (Devanagari digit 2), which is not an abbreviation in the book's ABBREVIATIONS FOR PARTS OF PLANTS table (roman abbreviation column at lines 876-937). Nothing in this entry's verse or numbering names a plant part for sariva, so the cell is illegible. Non-forcing observation, again NOT applied: the Sariva rows cited above print "(Rt.)" almost uniformly. (4) QUANTITY CORRECTED, "455 8." read as "455 g.": the digits 455 are printed clean and only the unit glyph is corrupt. The correction is forced because "8" is not a unit anywhere in this book — the book's only weight and volume units are g., kg. and l. (see the quantity column throughout, e.g. lines 20331-20332 and 20385-20388) — and the identical OCR substitution of "8." for "g." occurs in this same scan in other composition rows, e.g. line 12569 "9.6 8." and line 25947 "768 8." (17 such occurrences in the file). Of the three possible units only the single-character "g." matches the glyph shape and a solid drug measured in the same 455 as row 2's manjistha; "kg." is three characters and "l." is reserved for liquids in this book.

The prior transcription's claim that "Gite" is bleed from the neighbouring column is withdrawn as unevidenced: the right column on this line is occupied by entry 8:29's therapeutic-use text ("mutrakrechra; mudha vata; katitru-prstha"), so the token sits in row 5's own quantity slot and is most likely a garbled quantity. rows.name: Priyangu
rows.ocrCorrected: Quantity corrected, part left unresolved. Line 4580 prints exactly '(1.) 24 £. ' - the unit glyph is U+00A3 POUND SIGN (verified byte-for-byte: 28 31 2e 29 20 32 34 20 c2 a3 2e 20 0a). The quantity is corrected to '24 g.'; the printed numeral 24 is not altered, only the £ glyph is read as the unit g. Forced from inside the entry: verse line 4472 prints 'एषामर्धपलान्भागान्' (eSAm ardha-palAn bhAgAn, half a pala of each of the foregoing), which governs items 1-23, and this entry's own pala is fixed at 48 g by its printed dhataki figure of 480 g at line 4586 against verse line 4475's 'पलानि दश धातक्या' (palAni dasa dhAtakyA, ten pala of dhataki), so ardha-pala = 24 g, matching the printed numeral and leaving g. as the only unit the entry admits. Corroborated by the 22 sibling rows printing 24 g. and, outside the entry, by the same £-for-g. substitution elsewhere in this OCR, most plainly at line 5261 where one two-column line carries both forms ('11. Kramuka (piiga) (Sd.) 12 £. | 8. Citraka (Rt.) 48 g.') and at line 20363 ('25.6 £.'); that outside evidence is corroboration only and is not what forces the cell. The PART is NOT corrected: '(1.)' is not a defined abbreviation in the book's table (expansions 820-880, abbreviations 883-937), and neither the verse nor the numbering names a plant part for Priyangu, so the cell is transcribed as printed and the row flagged illegible. Priyangu prints as (Fl.) elsewhere in AFI Part I (e.g. lines 3701, 20234, 22701), but that lies outside this entry and does not force the cell.

rows.name: Draksa
rows.ocrCorrected: Quantity corrected from the printed '(Dr. Fr.) 22.880kg.' at line 4589 to '2.880 kg.'. Forced inside the entry: verse line 4475 prints 'पलानि दश धातक्या द्राक्षा षष्टिपला भवेत्‌' (palAni dasa dhAtakyA drAkSA SaSTipalA bhavet) - dhataki ten pala, draksa sixty pala. The printed dhataki quantity, 480 g. at line 4586, fixes this entry's pala at 48 g, so 60 pala = 2,880 g = 2.880 kg. Two further internal checks agree: verse line 4473 'गुडतुलाव्रयम्‌' (guDatulAtrayam, three tula) against the printed 14.400 kg at line 4584 gives 1 tula = 4.800 kg = 100 pala of 48 g, and verse line 4472 'अर्धपल' (ardha-pala) against the printed 24 g of items 1-23 gives the same 48 g pala. rows.name: Kantakari
rows.ocrCorrected: CORRECTED. Part cell prints "(P1.)" at line 4711 (digit one for letter l).
